problem: Discrete diffusion language models struggle to leverage low-confidence predictions during iterative denoising, missing opportunities for stronger evidence retrieval before output finalization.
approach: SARDI uses discarded low-confidence tokens as lookahead signals to guide retrieval-augmented generation dynamically during the denoising process, without requiring training or retraining the retriever.
contribution: Demonstrates that SARDI outperforms training-free diffusion and autoregressive retrieval baselines at up to 8× higher throughput across five multi-hop QA benchmarks.

problem: Existing 4D VAEs rely on 2D projections that create distortions and incomplete views, failing to preserve native 4D spatio-temporal relationships.
approach: Proposes a 4D VAE operating directly in dynamic voxel space with spatio-temporal window attention and differentiable voxel rendering loss to preserve explicit coordinates throughout encoding and decoding.
contribution: Improves 4D reconstruction fidelity over pointmap and flow-based VAEs while learning structurally consistent latent space, and enables training of video-conditioned 4D diffusion models.

problem: Evaluating whether structured reward shaping via RL can improve functional plasmid generation better than supervised fine-tuning.
approach: Compares SFT versus GRPO-based RL post-training for PlasmidGPT using biologically-motivated reward functions encoding annotations, length, and repeat penalties; includes reward ablation analysis.
contribution: RL achieves 71.6% quality-control pass rate versus 4.3% for pretrained baseline and 11.0% for SFT; identifies cassette arrangement bonus as critical reward component, and shows convergence toward real plasmid distributions on unmotivized features.

problem: Predicting whether ML model improvements in pCTR/pCVR prediction actually lead to better platform outcomes across diverse auction formats and bidder strategies.
approach: Formalizes model improvement via cluster refinement and systematically characterizes Evaluation Criteria Metrics monotonicity across bidder types (tCPA, max-CPA), auction formats (first-price, second-price, VCG), and budget constraints.
contribution: Shows first-price auctions with uniform bidding guarantee revenue monotonicity for tCPA bidders without budgets, while second-price auctions and budget constraints can break monotonicity, with full numerical constructions for non-monotonicity.

problem: Existing climate QA benchmarks are small, mostly text-only, and lack coverage of multimodal reasoning across scientific articles, videos, and figures.
approach: MMClima constructs a large-scale multimodal framework via automated claim extraction and QA synthesis with human validation, spanning text, video transcripts, and figures across five climate domains; includes fine-tuning of mmclima-70b-txt baseline.
contribution: Releases 104k+ expert-validated QA pairs and demonstrates that domain-adapted fine-tuning outperforms strong open and closed-source models on textual QA, enabling standardized multimodal climate evaluation.

problem: Neural operators and hybrid neural iterative schemes struggle with sparse linear systems from PDE discretization due to poor generalization across parameters and stagnation as residuals evolve.
approach: G-RANS performs residual-aware subspace corrections by mapping residuals to matrix graphs, generating multi-scale correction subspaces via a basis generator, and applying projected updates through differentiable projection; trained self-supervised via progressive bootstrap.
contribution: Achieves 10^-5 order residuals, substantially outperforming end-to-end neural operators, with 2-4× less wall-clock time than Krylov solvers, while showing robustness to ±70% coefficient shifts.

problem: Epidemic modeling relies on fixed model classes that require manual redesign when pathogens, policies, or scenarios evolve, hindering adaptive public health planning.
approach: EpiAgent synthesizes, calibrates, verifies, and refines epidemiological simulators via iterative program synthesis, using an explicit epidemiological flow graph for modular correctness checks before code generation.
contribution: Demonstrates capture of complex growth dynamics and produces epidemiologically consistent counterfactual projections across vaccination and immune escape assumptions; prevents model degeneration and accelerates convergence toward valid models.

problem: Consistency Models for one-step real-world image super-resolution struggle with consistency drift accumulation and geometric decoupling, where pixel-wise alignment fails to preserve structural coherence.
approach: GTASR introduces Trajectory Alignment via full-path projection to rectify tangent vector fields, and Dual-Reference Structural Rectification to enforce strict structural constraints within a consistency training paradigm.
contribution: Delivers superior performance over representative baselines while maintaining minimal latency, addressing both consistency drift and geometric decoupling in one-step super-resolution.

problem: Shampoo's expensive internal operations for computing inverse matrix roots create significant computational slowdown during training, limiting practical adoption.
approach: DASH stacks preconditioner blocks into 3D tensors for GPU utilization improvement and introduces Newton-DB iteration and Chebyshev polynomial approximations for faster inverse-root computation; includes matrix scaling analysis.
contribution: Achieves up to 5.6× faster optimizer steps versus optimized Distributed Shampoo, with Newton-DB attaining lowest validation perplexity per iteration among tested methods.

problem: Symbolic regression via LLMs is hindered by inefficient search strategies and coarse scalar feedback metrics that fail to identify which equation components drive performance or cause error.
approach: IGSR generates candidate basis functions with an LLM and evaluates them using granular influence scores quantifying each term's marginal contribution to generalization; integrates into Monte Carlo Tree Search for combinatorial search.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness on diverse benchmarks including LLM-SRBench and real-world genomic data; identifies novel relationship between DNA methylation and RNA Polymerase II pausing in a high-dimensional case study.

problem: Decoding-based regression suffers from misalignment between discrete token-level objectives and continuous numerical values, limiting precision and generalization.
approach: GenRe² formulates generation as a Markov decision process with sequence-level rewards for global numerical coherence; combines policy gradient methods and on-policy distillation for dense expert supervision.
contribution: Consistently outperforms traditional baselines across tabular regression, code metric prediction, and generative reward modeling, establishing robust paradigm for general-purpose numerical prediction.

problem: It remains unclear whether fundamental behavioral links exist between foundational LLMs and downstream multimodal variants in model lineages.
approach: Quantifies head-level context-truthfulness scores across LLM and MLLM lineages; proposes TruthProbe, a soft-gating strategy that amplifies context-truthful heads while preserving other contributions.
contribution: Shows Truth Scores are strongly preserved within model families despite instruction tuning or multimodal adaptation; TruthProbe improves contextual truthfulness on HaluEval and reduces multimodal hallucination on POPE and CHAIR.

problem: Multiple testing procedures must achieve asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity while remaining computationally tractable.
approach: Establishes asymptotic optimality of relative belief ratio (RBR) multiple testing rules under the two-groups model with additive 0-1 loss using a light-tailed normal prior.
contribution: Shows RBR rules achieve the same asymptotic Bayes risk as the oracle benchmark without relying on complex heavy-tailed priors, revealing an alternative inferential paradigm for sparsity.

problem: RL algorithms with function approximation achieve favorable sample complexity but often rely on computationally intractable oracles in low-rank MDPs.
approach: Establishes a hierarchy of RL oracles under low-rank MDPs and proposes an optimistic actor-critic algorithm relying solely on policy evaluation, avoiding expensive planning or optimization oracles.
contribution: Outperforms existing sample complexity guarantees for low-rank MDPs while being computationally tractable; extends to approximately low-rank MDPs and validates on standard Gym benchmarks.

problem: Learning stochastic dynamics from sparse temporal observations requires either high-frequency sampling or restrictive assumptions on conservative systems.
approach: Reformulates inference as stochastic control; uses geometry-driven path augmentation guided by the system's invariant density to reconstruct trajectories without assuming parametric models.
contribution: Accurately recovers overdamped Langevin dynamics from severely undersampled data, outperforming existing methods; demonstrates effectiveness of geometric inductive biases for stochastic system identification.

problem: Learning rate tuning via grid search is costly for large-scale models, and coarse grids lead to poor hyperparameter specification.
approach: Analyzes learning rate annealing schemes with polynomial decay (e.g., cosine schedule) in stochastic convex optimization, showing sublinear dependence on grid resolution misspecification factor.
contribution: Demonstrates convergence rate of O(ρ^(1/(2p+1))/√T) for annealed schedules versus O(ρ/√T) for fixed stepsize, achieving increased robustness to initial learning rate misspecification.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models exhibit brittleness on novel task distributions and struggle with superficial retrieval in in-context learning.
approach: RA-VLA integrates behavior-aligned context retrieval with grounded execution, enforcing faithful adherence to functional cues within scalable architecture.
contribution: Achieves superior success rates and computational efficiency on LIBERO benchmark and real UR5e environment; provides robust framework for training-free robotic adaptation.

problem: Existing image tokenizers excel at reconstruction fidelity but lack semantic structure, limiting performance on downstream generation tasks.
approach: Proposes tokenization framework with text-integrated encoder processing images and textual descriptions jointly, plus concept-guided training using sparse autoencoders to decompose vision-language features into semantic concepts.
contribution: Achieves rFID of 1.39 on ImageNet reconstruction, gFID of 2.65 on class-conditional generation, and 10.73 on text-to-image generation, bridging reconstruction-generation divide.

problem: Predicting numeric code outcomes (memory, latency, accuracy) requires extensive domain-specific feature engineering across diverse programming languages.
approach: Develops Regression Language Model using frozen LLM encoder to predict directly from text across memory footprint, GPU latency, neural network accuracy and speed.
contribution: A 300M parameter RLM achieves >0.9 Spearman-rank on APPS competitive programming and >0.5 average Spearman-rank across 24 programming languages; reaches 0.46 Kendall-Tau on NAS design spaces.

problem: LLMs hallucinate with high confidence on random facts lacking inferable patterns, but the root cause remains unclear.
approach: Formalizes memorization as a membership testing problem via rate-distortion theory, showing optimal strategy under limited capacity is to assign high confidence to non-facts rather than abstain.
contribution: Establishes rate-distortion theorem explaining hallucination as information-theoretic optimal behavior under lossy compression; validates on synthetic and real-world data.

problem: Statistical complexity of structure learning in graphical models remains unclear.
approach: Establishes reduction between structure learning and optimal conditional independence testing; demonstrates optimal algorithms via suitable modifications of the PC algorithm.
contribution: Shows minimax optimal structure learning rate is determined by minimax rate for conditional independence testing; provides unified framework with derived optimal rates for Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric models.

problem: PINNs training with MSE loss assumes independent Gaussian residuals, but actual residuals are heterogeneous and heavy-tailed, causing large residuals to dominate optimization.
approach: Adopts Student-t residual model with equivalent hierarchical EM algorithm alternating between weight estimation and weighted MSE optimization.
contribution: Bounding influence of extreme residuals and admits convergence guarantees under standard assumptions; demonstrates improved solution accuracy and robustness on diverse PDE benchmarks.

problem: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers suffer from concept omission where specified objects fail to emerge in generated images.
approach: Identifies characteristic omission signal in text embeddings via linear probing; proposes Omission Signal Intervention amplifying this signal to catalyze generation of missing concepts.
contribution: Significantly alleviates concept omission on FLUX.1-Dev and SD3.5-Medium even in extreme scenarios using minimal intervention.

problem: Deep Equilibrium Models offer constant memory for infinite-depth networks but incur significant inference latency due to iterative fixed-point solvers.
approach: C-DEQ leverages consistency distillation by casting iterative inference as ODE evolution; trains to consistently map intermediate states to fixed point for few-step inference.
contribution: Achieves 2-20× accuracy improvements over implicit DEQs under same few-step budget; facilitates flexible multi-step evaluation to trade computation for performance.

problem: Determining optimal data mixture for LLM pre-training is challenging, as existing approaches rely on unreliable tiny-scale proxies or prohibitively expensive large-scale exploration.
approach: DeMix decouples search from training by training component models and deriving mixture proxies via weighted model merging, enabling evaluation of unlimited sampled mixtures.
contribution: Breaks the trade-off between sufficiency, accuracy, and efficiency; obtains optimal mixture with higher benchmark performance at lower search cost; releases 22T-token DeMix Corpora.

problem: Spectral gradient methods like Muon show strong empirical gains but lack theoretical understanding of their mechanisms.
approach: Analyzes gradient descent and spectral gradient descent on phase retrieval with anisotropic inputs; shows spectral methods remove variance-induced misalignment during escape phase.
contribution: Demonstrates spectral gradient descent prevents anisotropic magnification effects, leading to stable alignment and accelerated noise contraction compared to standard gradient descent.

problem: In-context learning in Transformers fails sharply under distribution shift, reducing their practical deployment robustness.
approach: Studies attention temperature as inference-time control using high-dimensional linear regression framework with approximate softmax attention; derives closed-form expression for ICL error under distribution shift.
contribution: Shows optimal attention temperature minimizes generalization error and can recover near Bayes-optimal performance; validates on LLMs for question-answering under noisy demonstrations.

problem: Fast adversarial training suffers from Catastrophic Overfitting where robustness to multi-step attacks collapses despite high single-step performance.
approach: Formalizes Epsilon Overfitting perspective and proposes SORA with adaptive step-size adjustment based on perturbation alignment metric predicting overfitting onset.
contribution: Consistently prevents Catastrophic Overfitting achieving state-of-the-art robustness and clean accuracy; generalizes across datasets and architectures with single fixed hyperparameter set.

problem: Metrics measuring representational similarity are confounded by network scale, obscuring whether representations actually converge across models.
approach: Introduces permutation-based null-calibration framework transforming any representational similarity metric into calibrated score with statistical guarantees.
contribution: Reveals apparent Platonic convergence from global spectral measures largely disappears after calibration; proposes Aristotelian Representation Hypothesis showing convergence in local neighborhoods only.

problem: LLMs generate logically inconsistent outputs and enable reward hacking due to stochastic next-token prediction, limiting reasoning reliability.
approach: Introduces formal logic verification-guided framework dynamically interleaving symbolic verification with language generation; implements via two-stage training pipeline combining verification-guided SFT and policy optimization.
contribution: 7B and 14B models outperform state-of-the-art by average margins of 10.4% and 14.2% respectively across six reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Spiking Transformers lack principled temporal fusion mechanisms limiting their ability to exploit spatiotemporal dependencies.
approach: TEFormer achieves bidirectional temporal fusion through forward temporal fusion in attention module and backward gated recurrent structure in MLP, decoupling temporal modeling across components.
contribution: Consistently and significantly outperforms SNN and Spiking Transformer baselines across benchmarks; performance gains remain stable across diverse neural encoding schemes.

problem: Medical image segmentation in continual learning faces heterogeneous sequential tasks without predefined groupings, causing catastrophic forgetting and inefficient knowledge transfer.
approach: MedCRP-CL uses Chinese Restaurant Process for online task structure discovery from clinical text prompts; maintains semantic modality-specific LoRA adapters regularized by intra-modality EWC.
contribution: Achieves 73.3% Dice score with 4.1% forgetting, outperforming best baseline by 8.0% with 6× fewer parameters; discovers semantic modalities finer-grained than physical imaging modes.

problem: CLIP-based no-reference image quality assessment suffers from perceptual submergence where contrastive pretraining suppresses subtle perceptual signals.
approach: CMPA introduces Perception-Sensitive Feature Extractor projecting CLIP features into low-dimensional subspace and Cross-Modal Perception Alignment Injector with residual-enhanced downscaling.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on benchmark datasets by recovering perceptual signals submerged in semantic-dense representations.

problem: Mamba-based vision models with token reduction exhibit severe performance collapse due to spatially agnostic reduction violating two-dimensional structural requirements.
approach: STORM reformulates token reduction as structured operation on spatial units enforcing localized constraints to maintain grid topology and neighborhood coherence.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art training-free pruning with up to 63.3% accuracy recovery on VMamba; incurs only 1.0% drop on PlainMamba with performance comparable to ViT.

problem: LVLMs remain vulnerable to evasive backdoor attacks that corrupt compositional understanding of object relationships.
approach: TokenSwap injects visual triggers while swapping grammatical roles of key tokens in answers; uses adaptive token-weighted loss to emphasize learning on swapped tokens.
contribution: Achieves high attack success rates while maintaining evasiveness and stealthiness across multiple LVLM architectures by inducing bags-of-words behavior.

problem: Maximum Entropy RL with iterative generative policies (diffusion/flow matching) lacks access to action log-densities, complicating policy stochasticity regulation.
approach: FLAC formulates policy optimization as Generalized Schrödinger Bridge problem with kinetic energy regularization as proxy for divergence from high-entropy reference.
contribution: Achieves superior or comparable performance on high-dimensional benchmarks relative to strong baselines while avoiding explicit density estimation.

problem: LLM-translated code often runs significantly slower than human-written equivalents, and prompt engineering alone cannot remedy this issue.
approach: SwiftTrans comprises Multi-Perspective Exploration generating diverse candidates via parallel ICL and Difference-Aware Selection identifying optimal candidate by comparing translations.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements in both correctness and runtime efficiency across CodeNet, F2SBench, and new SwiftBench benchmark.

problem: Multimodal agents struggle to generalize in complex real-world tasks due to insufficient task-specific procedural knowledge.
approach: Proposes framework representing task knowledge as natural-language procedures and trains procedure-aware grounded agent conditioning actions on this knowledge from diverse sources.
contribution: Enables robust generalization across tasks, applications, interface versions, and multi-app workflows on challenging Android benchmarks.

problem: Existing class unlearning evaluations overlook class geometry allowing information leakage about forgotten classes through neighboring class probabilities.
approach: Introduces Class Membership Inference Attack and proposes Tilted REWeighting distribution matching retrained-from-scratch model by approximating inter-class similarity.
contribution: TREW reduces gap with retrained models by 19% and 46% on CIFAR-10 for U-LiRA and CMIA scores respectively while matching/surpassing existing metrics.

problem: Graph collaborative filtering using contrastive learning objectives like Sampled Softmax exhibits unclear optimization dynamics regarding neighbor pair upweighting.
approach: Analyzes GCF prediction mechanism by unfolding aggregation over neighbor pairs; identifies that effective optimization depends on selectively upweighting structurally similar neighbor pairs.
contribution: Proposes NT-SSM with type-aware neighbor pair weight update dynamics, achieving consistent performance improvements over SSM across datasets and GCF models.
